heading: INT. RUDDY & GREEN BUILDING - ELEVATOR
summary: Mid-30s Rose, wearing a Tim Hortons uniform with messy hair and blood on her face, catches her breath beside the far bloodier Mariner while romantic muzak plays. She picks up a bloody scrap with hair, snorts, drops it, and asks whether it is skull. Mariner's face, beard, red cap, and mask are described before a full-screen title card introduces him; after he confirms that the scrap is skull, the screenplay details his moss-green sweater, anchor bracers, Dad tattoo, shell-and-fish-hook bandolier, tall boots, weighted fishing-net cape, and bloodied metal-edged oar. Mariner admits that he hid an AirTag in Rose's purse at Thanksgiving; when he assumes the armed men targeted her because of him, Rose laughs and challenges that assumption. Three armed thugs attack when the doors open on twelve, and Mariner deflects a gun with his oar and kicks one thug into the others while Rose closes the doors under gunfire. After a thug orders the group down to eight, Rose chooses eleven so she and Mariner can take the stairs back up, then silently questions his outfit before he calls it functional and an homage.

narrative_beats.description: Rose is introduced in a Tim Hortons uniform with messy hair and blood on her face while romantic muzak plays; she handles a bloody scrap with hair and asks whether it is skull.

The source describes the much bloodier Mariner's face, beard, red cap, and mask, presents a full-screen title card naming him, then has him confirm that the scrap is skull before detailing his moss-green sweater, anchor bracers, Dad tattoo, shell-and-fish-hook bandolier, tall boots, weighted fishing-net cape, and bloodied metal-edged oar.
Mariner admits he stashed an AirTag in Rose's purse at Thanksgiving, and Rose realizes the purse was left behind.
Rose and Mariner argue about returning for the purse and whether the armed men targeted her because of him.
Rose laughs at Mariner's belief that the attackers went after her because of him, implying that his assumption about their target is wrong.
Three armed thugs confront them on twelve; Mariner uses his oar and a kick to break the attack while Rose closes the elevator doors under gunfire.
After a muffled thug orders the group down to eight, Rose sends the elevator to eleven so she and Mariner can take the stairs up, showing improvisational resolve despite his objection.
Rose raises an eyebrow at Mariner's strange costume, and he insists that it is functional and an homage.

tone_mood: darkly comic, tense, intimate, and violently kinetic
